answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a slow, unique proof of work: before an identity may transact, it must finish a sequential computation bound to its own key. Like carving a glacier, it cannot be rushed by parallel machines, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the compute. New identities also face a basalt-hard cap inside a shared vault: funds they receive stay time-locked and unlock gradually only as verified work accumulates, so a fake swarm can neither drain value quickly nor fake reputation at scale.
